notes: Chart 'Notes:' field: stiff west wind at ridge elevation. Wind Loading: yes. Layer Notes as printed in the JPG: 132-129cm: March 2; 120-119.5cm: Feb 26; 71-70cm: Feb 3; 12-5cm: sintering. The PDF overlays corrected text on the two dated notes (header block and right-hand comment column): 132-129cm: April 2; 120-119.5cm: March 26 (these corrected dates are used in named_layers). Stability tests column: CT23, RP@120cm; CT24, RP@120cm. Specifics and Stability fields blank.
summary: Basal DH 0-39 cm (3-8 mm, 1F to P) with a P FCxr band at 28-34 cm, under FCxr 39-80 cm (4F at 39-58, 1F+/P above) holding a thin I-hard IF crust at 70-71 cm (Feb 3); RG 80-120 cm (P+/P at 80-110, 1F+, 1F) split by a K MFcr at 110-112 cm and a 0.5 cm 4F FC layer at 119.5-120 cm (March 26 layer; CT23 and CT24 RP at 120 cm); K MFcr at 129-132 cm (April 2) under 18 cm of DF (4F+ then F); DF 3 mm on the surface; HS 150 cm; snow -0.5 C at the ground to -3.5 C at 120 cm, air -6 C
reading_issues: JPG and PDF carry the same SnowPilot image (pixel analyses agree to +-1 px, so one JSON with both source files). The only difference is the PDF's overlaid text boxes, which replace 'March 2' with 'April 2' (132-129 cm) and 'Feb 26' with 'March 26' (120-119.5 cm) in both the header Layer Notes block and the right-hand comment column; the corrected PDF dates are used in named_layers and the originals are kept in notes. Hardness bars, boundaries and temperature dots were measured from native pixels (hardness ticks every 24 px = 1/3 step; HS line at y=157 and ground at y=751 give 3.96 px/cm); boundaries are rounded to integer cm (measured within 0.2 cm), except the 0.5 cm layer at 119.5-120 cm whose bounds follow its layer note. The 95-110 cm layer is a trapezoid (P+ at base to P- at top) and hardness_idx is the mean. Glyphs: two linked circles on K layers read as MFcr (110-112 and 129-132 cm); the filled rectangle on the I-hard 70-71 cm layer read as IF; square-with-rounded-top read as FCxr; slash read as DF. The form-table rows are stretched for thin layers (connector lines), so rows were matched to layers by order (20 layers, 20 rows plus the zero-thickness surface row). The temperature line has no dots at 110 or 130 cm. Aspect field is blank; 'flat' is assumed from the 0 deg slope. The two CT failures at 120 cm sit at the top of the thin FC layer (layer_grain FC).
